reason: The reflector petals and receiver appear to be the main parts of the solar furnace.
expectation: The petals will concentrate sunlight onto the receiver to form the furnace.

alternatives.reason: Screening the spoil also looks useful for preparing feedstock.

effect: The petals cannot yet be joined to the receiver; their listed partner is steel.
reaction: I was surprised the furnace parts do not combine directly.
reason: Steel is the confirmed partner for the reflector petals, likely providing their support.
expectation: The steel will support the reflector petals as part of the furnace.

alternatives.reason: Screening the spoil could advance the feedstock goal instead.

effect: Steel provided the support needed to assemble the reflector; the receiver may now fit it.
reaction: The braced ring makes the assembly sequence clearer.
reason: The supported reflector and receiver are the remaining apparent furnace components.
expectation: The receiver will attach to the reflector to complete or advance the solar furnace.

alternatives.reason: Screening the regolith could advance the feedstock goal.

effect: The receiver completed the solar furnace, leaving feedstock preparation as the remaining goal.
reaction: The focused sunlight makes the furnace's purpose clear.
reason: The screening mesh should separate usable fine material from the excavated regolith.
expectation: The mesh will produce screened regolith suitable for further forming.

effect: The mesh needs steel before it can be used with the regolith.
reaction: That repeats the support-building pattern from the reflector.
reason: Steel is the mesh's confirmed partner and may provide a supporting frame.
expectation: The steel will support the mesh so it can screen regolith.

effect: The steel and mesh made a rigid sieve, ready to screen the excavated regolith.
reaction: The rim and collection tray make the preparation step physically clear.
reason: The sieve is made for separating fine material from the excavated spoil.
expectation: The sieve will separate fine regolith for feedstock preparation.

effect: The sieve separated out coarse stones, leaving screened regolith ready for forming.
reaction: The screening step makes the feedstock's consistency clear.
reason: The workshop press is the apparent place to form the screened feedstock.
expectation: The press will form the screened regolith into a feedstock shape.

effect: The press formed supported, unfired blanks and completed the remaining goal; firing would still be needed to give them strength.
reaction: The distinction between shaping and strength was a useful, satisfying detail.

mostWorthwhile.text: Pressing the screened regolith was the most worthwhile passage: it connected grading and forming to a clear explanation of why the blanks still need firing.

leastWorthwhile.text: The failed attempts to combine the obvious working parts directly were repetitive, although their compatibility feedback revealed the needed supports.

surprise.text: I initially expected the reflector petals and receiver to combine directly; discovering that the petals first needed a steel support changed my understanding of the assembly sequence.

arbitrary.text: The mesh needing steel before screening initially felt like an unstated prerequisite, but the resulting rigid rim and collection tray gave it a physical purpose.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see how the blanks are fired and used, especially because the chapter explained the material preparation in physically meaningful terms.
